def smallest_change(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    changed = [False] * n
    count = 0
    for i in range(n // 2):
        j = n - 1 - i
        if nums[i] != nums[j]:
            # Change one of them (only one change counted)
            # Mark the changed element; to minimize changes, change the one not already changed
            # If neither changed, change one; if one already changed, change the other
            # But since starting fresh, just count one change per differing pair
            # To count number of elements changed, we need to mark which element changed
            # We'll pick to change the element that hasn't been changed yet; if both unmarked, pick i
            # This logic avoids double counting changes
            if not changed[i] and not changed[j]:
                changed[i] = True
                count += 1
            elif changed[i] and not changed[j]:
                changed[j] = True
                count += 1
            elif not changed[i] and changed[j]:
                changed[i] = True
                count += 1
            # if both changed, no new change needed (unlikely)
    return count
